Lemma
[second-order necessary condition at a minimum]

1. ch9:3.1If $f:\mathbf{R}\to \mathbf{R}$ has a local minimum at $x$, is continuous there and is twice differentiable at $x$, then $f''(x)\ge 0$. This is the step by which a minimizing geodesic forces $E_j''(0)\ge 0$ in section 2: each curve of the variation joins the same endpoints, so $E_j(s)\ge E_j(0)$, i.e. $s=0$ is a minimum of $E_j$.
Proof

\sketch If $f''(x)<0$, then for sufficiently small $h\ne 0$ the symmetric second difference $f(x+h)+f(x-h)-2f(x)$ is negative. One of $f(x+h)$ and $f(x-h)$ is therefore smaller than $f(x)$, contradicting local minimality.

□
